sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers the north-western part of Bogota at 100 ft to an inch, from South Street at the top to Munn Avenue at the bottom and from the Hackensack River on the west to a short way east of Elm Avenue. The western third is the river front: the West Shore Railroad (New York Central and Hudson River) runs diagonally down the sheet with its sidings and a coal trestle, and between the tracks and the river lie the Hackensack Coal and Lumber Co. coal pockets and yards, the Bogota Planing Mill Co., an oil company's tank yard and the Valvoline Oil Co. dock, the J. N. Wolfe sash, door and blind factory, the Standard Key Manufacturing Co., the Felter Coal and Lumber Co. elevator and lumber sheds, and a boat club on Hackensack and Fort Lee Road where it runs down to the river. A ball park lies at the top left. East of River Road the sheet is a residential grid of mostly two-storey frame dwellings on River Road, Orchard Terrace, Larch Avenue and Elm Avenue, crossed by Main (Maple) Street, West Broad (School) Street, Hackensack and Fort Lee Road and McDougal Lane. Public and commercial buildings include the Bogota School on Main Street at River Road, the Borough Hall on West Broad Street, a fire department station, a row of stores at Elm Avenue and Fort Lee Road (drugs, groceries, fruit, a bank, meats), the Bogart Memorial Reformed Church with its community house and rectory on Larch Avenue, and the Bogota Water and Light Co. pumping station at Munn Avenue. The upper left carries the town's water facilities and fire department notes, which are masked out.
notes: Main (Maple) is West Main Street today; W. Broad (School) is West Broad Street.
Hackensack and Fort Lee Road is West Fort Lee Road today.
McDougal Lane (Linden) is Mc Dougall Lane in OpenStreetMap; Division Street is Linden Avenue.
River Road / West Main Street carries a 4.6 m residual: the detected point is on the drawn centre, so the modern node is probably off the old line.
Water facilities and fire department text at the upper left is cut out of the mask.

Scale 100 ft. North-central Bogota: River Rd, Orchard Ter, Larch Av, Elm Av, Division (now Linden Av) between South St and Munn Av; Main (Maple) = West Main St, W. Broad (School) = West Broad St, Hackensack & Ft Lee Rd = West Fort Lee Rd, McDougal Lane (Linden) = Mc Dougall Lane. West strip: West Shore RR, coal and lumber yards, Hackensack River. One part; water facilities and fire department text notched out of the mask.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 is drawn turned on the page, with north to the right, at 100 ft to an inch. It covers central Bogota and the adjoining edge of Teaneck Township between West Shore Avenue (top, with the West Shore Railroad freight house and passenger station) and Queen Ann Road (bottom), and between Munn (Elmwood) Avenue on the left and Leonia Avenue, Preston Street and East Main (Maple) Street on the right. The streets running across the page are West Shore, Leonia, Ridgefield, Summit and Palisade avenues and, in Teaneck, Crestview, James and Pleasant places; Linwood Avenue, Central Avenue, West End Avenue, Bogert Street, Hackensack and Fort Lee Road, Hill Street and 1st to 4th places run down the page. The business centre is at Leonia Avenue near the station: groceries, an office, news, a bank, paints, a bakery, a Chinese laundry, a garage, hardware, and the Regent Motion Pictures theatre with storage, grocery and notions stores. Palisade Avenue has St. Joseph's Catholic Church and Palisade Avenue Public School No. 2; Central Avenue has Fire Department Station No. 2 of the Bogota Heights Hose Co., and Linwood Avenue a Lutheran church. The rest is frame dwellings, many lots still empty, with house numbers and block numbers (Teaneck blocks 694 to 696). The Bogota-Teaneck borough line follows Fort Lee Road and a dash-dot line across the right side, which is otherwise blank.
notes: The sheet is turned: north points to the right (fitted rotation about 74 degrees).
Hackensack and Fort Lee Road is East Fort Lee Road and Fort Lee Road today; Queen Ann Road is Queen Anne Road; High View is Highview Place.
Cedar Place (Hawthorne Place) is Dunn Avenue today.
Three Fort Lee Road junctions were measured from edge pairs narrower than the parcels (residuals 2.7 to 3.7 m).
Regent Motion Pictures theatre on Leonia Avenue; St. Joseph's Catholic Church and Palisade Avenue Public School No. 2 on Palisade Avenue.

Scale 100 ft. Turned sheet: north points right (rotation about +74). Central Bogota and Teaneck edge between West Shore Av and Queen Ann Rd, Elmwood/Munn Av and Leonia Av: Ridgefield, Summit, Palisade, West End, Bogert, Linwood, Central, Hill, Preston, 1st-4th Pl, Crestview, James, Pleasant, E. Main (Maple), High View. One part.

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 covers south-western Bogota at 100 ft to an inch, from Munn Avenue at the top to North Avenue and the Ridgefield Park line at the bottom, and from the Hackensack River on the west to Palisade Avenue on the east. The eastern half is a regular residential grid between West Shore Avenue and Palisade Avenue, crossed by Beechwood, Walnut, Oakwood, Maplewood, Chestnut, Cypress (lettered Cyress) and Fairview avenues, with frame dwellings concentrated in the northern blocks and many unbuilt lots to the south; the Bogota Water Co. standpipe stands on Munn Avenue. The West Shore Railroad runs down the middle of the sheet. West of it the land is largely open, laid out along River Road, Charles Street, Cross Street and Bergen Avenue with a few dwellings, a pond and a brook. The south-west is industrial, beside the river: the Bogota Paper and Board Company (paper making, beating engines, cylinder paper machine, storage of baled paper), the Continental Paper Company, manufacturers of box board (reinforced concrete fire-proof stock house, screen room, beater engine building), and the Federal Paper Company (beating engines, calendering and finishing, cylinder machine room, box shop, lining and shipping room), linked by sidings. Printed notes on the three mills' fire protection are masked out. River Road at the bottom becomes West Shore Avenue's southern continuation by Fairview Avenue.
notes: Cypress Avenue is lettered Cyress Avenue.
West Shore Avenue was left out of the control: its modern centre lies about 25 ft (7 to 8 m) west of the drawn centre, and the detector paired lines of the railroad strip.
Charles Street, Cross Street and Bergen Avenue west of the railroad are not in the modern street network.
Bogota Paper and Board Company, Continental Paper Company and Federal Paper Company mills by the river.

Scale 100 ft. South-west Bogota: Palisade Av to West Shore Av between Munn Av and North Av, plus River Rd, Charles, Cross, Bergen Av and the Bogota Paper & Board, Federal Paper and Continental Paper mills by the Hackensack River. One part; three printed text blocks notched out of the mask. Modern West Shore Avenue lies about 25 ft west of the drawn centre: left out.

sheet-36-1.description: The main map of sheet 36 covers south-eastern Bogota at 100 ft to an inch, from Elmwood Avenue at the top to North Avenue and the Ridgefield Park boundary at the bottom, and from Palisade Avenue (lettered Munn Avenue at its northern end) on the west to Queen Ann Road and the Teaneck Township line on the east. It is a regular grid of long blocks crossed by Elmwood, Beechwood, Walnut, Oakwood, Maplewood, Chestnut, Cypress and Fairview avenues, with Hawthorne Place and Cedar Place running north and south and Valley View Place near North Avenue. The northern blocks are closely built with numbered two-storey frame dwellings, many marked with private garages; south of Oakwood Avenue most lots are laid out but empty. Across Queen Ann Road, in Teaneck, the sheet shows Walnut, Oak and Maple streets with a few houses, a machine shop with electric power at Henry Street, and stores near North Avenue. Below North Avenue the first blocks of Ridgefield Park are indicated only by the ends of 2nd to 8th streets and Arthur Street. The upper left corner is taken by the inset (part 2) and the area above Elmwood Avenue in the middle is left blank, belonging to sheet 33.
notes: Hawthorne Place is Fischer Avenue north of Maplewood Avenue and Fisher Avenue south of it today; the drawn jog at Maplewood matches.
Cedar Place is Dunn Avenue today; its junctions carried 3 to 4.5 m residuals and it was left out of the control.
Queen Ann Road is Queen Anne Road.

Scale 100 ft. South-east Bogota: Palisade Av to Queen Ann Rd between Elmwood Av and North Av (Hawthorne Pl = Fischer/Fisher Av, Cedar Pl = Dunn Av, Dunn left out as displaced). Two parts: 1 main map; 2 inset top left (block 44A, Herman Encke florist, Queen Ann Rd between Ft Lee Rd and Henry St), placed by three hand-picked points along Queen Anne Road (helmert, low confidence).

sheet-36-2.description: Inset in the upper left corner of sheet 36, at the sheet's scale of 100 ft to an inch with its own north arrow. It shows block 44A in Teaneck Township, the triangle bounded by Queen Ann Road on the west, Fort Lee Road on the north and Henry Street on the south, opposite the end of Central Avenue. The block is the nursery of Herman Encke, florist: a long glass-roofed green house, a smaller green house and sheds (marked to be removed) along Fort Lee Road, and several dwellings with garages facing Queen Ann Road (numbers 99 to 113), including a grocery at the Fort Lee Road corner. A 30 inch water pipe runs along Queen Ann Road. The inset continues the drawing of sheet 33, whose Queen Ann Road and Central Avenue it adjoins.
notes: Herman Encke, florist: green houses on block 44A.
Placed by three hand-picked points along Queen Anne Road (helmert); the inset is drawn about 7 degrees off its own north arrow, so position is good to a few metres and orientation is less certain.

Scale 100 ft. South-east Bogota: Palisade Av to Queen Ann Rd between Elmwood Av and North Av (Hawthorne Pl = Fischer/Fisher Av, Cedar Pl = Dunn Av, Dunn left out as displaced). Two parts: 1 main map; 2 inset top left (block 44A, Herman Encke florist, Queen Ann Rd between Ft Lee Rd and Henry St), placed by three hand-picked points along Queen Anne Road (helmert, low confidence).
